@wowsuchcurrency @sodogetip I might be turning off at least one of those Dogecoin Core nodes on server4you as it is getting very little traffic.

I do not use the "mishaboar" name on nodes in my home/office to avoid revealing my location via my IP.

Running a node is easy, but it requires a good unmetered Internet connection (I use 1TB per month on many nodes), and at least 65GB of space on disk.

You also need to open port 22556 in your router and firewall. 

You can get #Dogecoin Core from https://t.co/39RN3VnPDn.

Additionally, a node does:

- Provide redundancy to the network by providing more bandwidth, which could be critical during spikes in activity
- Establish a baseline for fees and dust limits through setting relay policies (since Dogecoin Core v1.14.4)

(2/2)
@TheOnlyFronk On a note, I do agree your method is reasonably safe for most people - I did go this route for many years and I still hold some Doge in a Dogecoin Core wallet backup.

@TheOnlyFronk I think the best strategy if you want to be 100% safe and you do not plan on spending your #Dogecoin often is to use the strategies u/Fulvio55 talks about on reddit, which involve no wallet software at all.

Not for the newbies, unfortunately.

While if you deploy #Dogecoin Core on an infected PC and generate a wallet with it, keyloggers and trojans might steal your wallet information, alongside the encryption password, while you are generating it.

So make sure the PC is 100% clean before generating the wallet. (2/2)

An important note.

In comparison with generating a wallet with #Dogecoin Core, hardware wallets like Ledger have one big  advantage. 

You could use them on a compromised PC, and your crypto should still be safe, since the private key is never accessible to the PC. (1/2)

In the case of an encrypted wallet, it is VITAL that. alongside the wallet.dat file, you also store the encryption password with the same care.

Unfortunately many people lost their #Dogecoin because they could not retrieve the encryption password.

Yes, as I mentioned many times: #Dogecoin Core, which you can download from https://t.co/39RN3VnPDn, is also a wallet.

It is still a "hot" wallet, but you can use it to encrypt the wallet and then store a copy of the wallet on multiple USB sticks not connected to the Internet.

My strategy (I omit some details for safety reasons):

- Long term #Dogecoin holding on multiple Ledger Nano (cheap and safe)
- Short term holding/day to day on MyDoge/Coinbase Wallet
- Backups split in multiple locations
- Only tiny amounts on custodial services like sodogetip

Always remember to have a good backup strategy. When you hold #Dogecoin in your own wallet, you are responsible for it. 

Store multiple copies of the private keys/seed phrases in multiple locations and devices NOT connected to the internet.

https://t.co/Nlv4JtCtdi

Wallets like Ledger/Trezor are also non-custodial. But with these wallets, aka as "cold" wallets, your private key is kept away from the outside world at all times thanks to the way the hardware/software is designed.

This makes them ideal for long term holding of your #Dogecoin.

Keep your #Dogecoin away from exchanges!

- Smartphone wallets like MyDoge are good for holding small amounts for day to day expenses, like tipping and buying McCannoli
- Large amounts/long term holding on cold wallet solutions like Ledger/Trezor
- Not your keys, not your #Doge! https://t.co/A4vSaKLI85

But how "safe" is #Dogecoin when you hold it in your private wallet? 

The core of the problem in this case is having proper backups. And proper backups are not just "ultra-safe" ones, but also those where you do not lose access to your funds because you forgot a password.

Fiat balances in exchanges holding your crypto in FDIC-insured banks are covered, usually up to 250k per bank (Coinbase, Gemini, RH offer this, for example).

In the case of RH, also securities (like stocks) are covered by the SIPC up to 500k. #Dogecoin

https://t.co/NgSb0Gf5uj

On a note, also services like Gemini Earn, of which I talked about for a long time, offer NO insurance on your crypto.

Not only that, in case of crypto lending platforms like Gemini you bear the full risk of the loans; so if the borrower can't pay, you lose everything. #Dogecoin

Note that not all exchanges offer this kind of insurance, and any promise to make you whole might be worth a lot less in case of an exchange acting in a completely unregulated framework and not part of a publicly traded company. #Dogecoin

From @coinbase: "In case of a covered security event, we will endeavor to make you whole. However, total losses may exceed insurance recoveries so your funds may still be lost. " #Dogecoin
